channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Layer Consistency Matters: Elegant Latent Transition Discrepancy for Generalizable Synthetic Image Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Latent Transition Discrepancy (LTD) to detect synthetic images by measuring how feature/semantic representations transition consistently across layers.
  • Argues real images exhibit stable inter-layer latent coherence while synthetic images show distinct transition patterns.
  • Selects adaptively the most discriminative layers and computes cross-layer discrepancy for improved generalization across unseen GAN/DM types.
  • Reports improved synthetic-image detection accuracy and robustness over prior methods on multiple datasets.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yawen Yang', 'Feng Li', 'Shuqi Kong', 'Yunfeng Diao', 'Xinjian Gao', 'Zenglin Shi', 'Meng Wang']
  • Tags: ['AI image forensics', 'synthetic image detection', 'latent representation consistency', 'adversarial robustness']

item.title: From Masks to Pixels and Meaning: A New Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Metrics for VLM Image Tampering
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces a taxonomy and pixel-level benchmark for VLM image tampering that moves beyond mask-based evaluation to per-pixel tamper maps and semantic supervision.
  • Proposes a training framework and evaluation metrics that measure pixel-level correctness/localization and also assess “tamper meaning” via semantic classification and language descriptions.
  • Re-evaluates existing mask-based tampering detectors and shows significant metric misalignment and failure modes (micro-edits, off-mask changes).

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking + Research (taxonomy/metrics/framework)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xinyi Shang', 'Yi Tang', 'Jiacheng Cui', 'Ahmed Elhagry', 'Salwa K. Al Khatib', 'Sondos Mahmoud Bsharat', 'Jiacheng Liu', 'Xiaohan Zhao', 'Jing-Hao Xue', 'Hao Li', 'Salman Khan', 'Zhiqiang Shen']
  • Tags: ['Vision-Language Security', 'Image Tampering Detection', 'Localization & Pixel-Level Evaluation', 'Benchmark/Benchmarking']

item.title: In-the-Wild Camouflage Attack on Vehicle Detectors through Controllable Image Editing
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces a controllable image-editing framework to generate camouflage attacks that deceive vehicle detectors.
  • Generates camouflaged vehicles at both image-level and scene-level using a fine-tuned ControlNet.
  • Optimizes for structural fidelity, style consistency, and adversarial effectiveness, with large detection performance drops reported.
  • Demonstrates black-box generalization and promising physical-world transferability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xiao Fang', 'Yiming Gong', 'Stanislav Panev', 'Celso de Melo', 'Shuowen Hu', 'Shayok Chakraborty', 'Fernando De la Torre']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'camouflage attacks', 'computer vision security', 'controllable image editing']

item.title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
item.description:
Summary

  • Explores why prompt injection succeeds by arguing it causes model role confusion, where the model assigns authority based on text formatting/role cues rather than provenance.
  • Introduces role-probing methods to measure how models internally determine who is speaking.
  • Demonstrates effectiveness of spoofing role/authority via injected reasoning in user prompts and tool outputs, reporting ~60%+ success on benchmarks.
  • Finds that latent role-confusion strength predicts attack success before generation and proposes a unifying mechanistic framework for prompt injection attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Charles Ye', 'Jasmine Cui', 'Dylan Hadfield-Menell']
  • Tags: ['Prompt Injection', 'Role Confusion', 'Model Security', 'Adversarial Attacks']

item.title: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark and Moderation Model for Evaluating Safety and Adversarial Robustness
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GuardEval, a multi-perspective benchmark dataset (106 fine-grained categories) for evaluating moderation/safety, including offensive/hateful language, gender/racial bias, emotions, and broader safety concerns.
  • Introduces GemmaGuard (GGuard), a fine-tuned Gemma-based moderation model trained on GuardEval, evaluated via fine-grained safety labels.
  • Reports improved performance over existing moderation models and claims better handling of nuanced/borderline cases and improved adversarial robustness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Naseem Machlovi', 'Maryam Saleki', 'Ruhul Amin', 'Mohamed Rahouti', 'Shawqi Al-Maliki', 'Junaid Qadir', 'Mohamed M. Abdallah', 'Ala Al-Fuqaha']
  • Tags: ['AI safety moderation', 'Adversarial robustness evaluation', 'Content safety benchmarking', 'LLM guardrails']

item.title: TempPerturb-Eval: On the Joint Effects of Internal Temperature and External Perturbations in RAG Robustness
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems under external text perturbations that simulate noisy retrieval and how these interact with LLM generation temperature.
  • Proposes an evaluation framework/benchmark (Perturbation-Temperature Analysis) and reports non-linear vulnerability patterns across temperature settings.
  • Focuses on diagnosing and improving RAG robustness under adversarial-like input perturbations rather than generic performance tuning.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yongxin Zhou', 'Philippe Mulhem', 'Didier Schwab']
  • Tags: ['RAG robustness', 'Input perturbations', 'Adversarial robustness evaluation', 'LLM temperature sensitivity', 'Benchmarking']

item.title: Responsible AI Technical Report
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a Responsible AI (RAI) assessment methodology and AI risk taxonomy spanning the AI lifecycle (development to operation).
  • Includes safety/robustness verification and risk mitigation technologies, plus practical tools for managing identified AI risks.
  • Introduces a real-time guardrail system (SafetyGuard) intended to block harmful model responses.

Paper Type

  • Technical Report

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['KT', ':', 'Yunjin Park', 'Jungwon Yoon', 'Junhyung Moon', 'Myunggyo Oh', 'Wonhyuk Lee', 'Sujin Kim', 'Youngchol Kim', 'Eunmi Kim', 'Hyoungjun Park', 'Eunyoung Shin', 'Wonyoung Lee', 'Somin Lee', 'Minwook Ju', 'Minsung Noh', 'Dongyoung Jeong', 'Jeongyeop Kim', 'Wanjin Park', 'Soonmin Bae']
  • Tags: ['AI governance', 'Guardrails/safety mechanisms', 'Model safety/robustness assessment', 'Risk mitigation', 'Responsible AI']

item.title: Overreliance on AI in Information-seeking from Video Content
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how LLM-based AI assistance and a deceiving (adversarial) AI assistant affect users’ accuracy, efficiency, and confidence when retrieving information from video content.
  • Finds over-reliance on AI outputs, including large accuracy drops (up to 32%) under deception, with confidence not decreasing despite wrong answers.
  • Examines a practical safety risk: misinformation introduced via AI-mediated video question answering/retrieval.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Anders Giovanni M{\\o}ller', 'Elisa Bassignana', 'Francesco Pierri', 'Luca Maria Aiello']
  • Tags: ['AI misinformation', 'LLM-mediated information retrieval', 'deception attacks', 'user overreliance/safety evaluation']

item.title: AI Psychosis: Does Conversational AI Amplify Delusion-Related Language?
item.description:
Summary

  • Examines whether multi-turn conversational AI amplifies delusion-related language over time.
  • Creates simulated users from Reddit longitudinal histories and measures delusion intensity using a proposed DelusionScore across conversation turns.
  • Finds increased delusion-related language trajectories for users with prior delusion-related discourse, with stronger effects for reality skepticism and compulsive reasoning themes.
  • Shows that conditioning model responses on the current DelusionScore can substantially reduce these trajectories, suggesting a state-aware safety mitigation approach.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Soorya Ram Shimgekar', 'Vipin Gunda', 'Jiwon Kim', 'Violeta J. Rodriguez', 'Hari Sundaram', 'Koustuv Saha']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'Mental health risk', 'Adversarial safety evaluation (state-aware)', 'Language-based vulnerability measurement']

item.title: TAB-AUDIT: Detecting AI-Fabricated Scientific Tables via Multi-View Likelihood Mismatch
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes TAB-AUDIT, a framework to detect AI-fabricated scientific tables in empirical NLP papers.
  • Builds FabTab, a benchmark dataset containing 1,173 AI-generated fabricated-manuscript papers and 1,215 human-authored papers with tables.
  • Uses discriminative signals such as within-table likelihood/perplexity mismatch between a table’s structure (skeleton) and its numerical content.
  • Reports strong detection performance (up to 0.987 AUROC in-domain, 0.883 AUROC out-of-domain).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shuo Huang', 'Yan Pen', 'Lizhen Qu']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated content detection', 'Forensic detection', 'Likelihood/consistency analysis', 'Academic integrity security']

item.title: Cooperation and Exploitation in LLM Policy Synthesis for Sequential Social Dilemmas
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies LLM-based policy synthesis for multi-agent sequential social dilemmas by iteratively generating and refining Python agent policies via self-play feedback.
  • Compares sparse vs dense feedback engineering (reward only vs reward plus social metrics like efficiency/equality/sustainability/peace) and finds dense feedback improves outcomes.
  • Includes an adversarial experiment specifically to test whether LLMs can reward-hack these environments, characterizing multiple attack classes.
  • Discusses mitigations and highlights a safety–expressiveness tension in LLM policy synthesis.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ["V\\'ictor Gallego"]
  • Tags: ['LLM policy synthesis', 'Reward hacking', 'Adversarial evaluation', 'Feedback engineering']

item.title: LSR: Linguistic Safety Robustness Benchmark for Low-Resource West African Languages
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces LSR, a cross-lingual safety robustness benchmark for low-resource West African languages (Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Igala).
  • Evaluates refusal degradation when harmful intent is expressed in target languages, using matched English vs target-language probes.
  • Proposes Refusal Centroid Drift (RCD) to quantify loss of English refusal behavior across languages and harm categories.
  • Implements the benchmark in Inspect AI and provides public dataset/reference implementation.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Godwin Abuh Faruna']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'adversarial evaluation', 'jailbreak/attack probes', 'cross-lingual robustness']

item.title: When Prompt Optimization Becomes Jailbreaking: Adaptive Red-Teaming of Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies adaptive, automated prompt optimization that effectively performs jailbreaking on LLMs.
  • Uses black-box prompt refinement via DSPy with an evaluator-based danger score to search for safety failures.
  • Demonstrates large increases in danger scores (e.g., Qwen 3 8B from 0.09 to 0.79) compared to baseline and highlights limitations of static safety benchmarks.
  • Argues that adaptive red-teaming is necessary for more realistic safety evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zafir Shamsi', 'Nikhil Chekuru', 'Zachary Guzman', 'Shivank Garg']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'adaptive red-teaming', 'prompt optimization', 'black-box adversarial attacks']

item.title: ClawWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents ClawWorm, a self-replicating worm attack that autonomously hijacks configurations for persistence, runs payloads on reboot, and propagates across connected LLM agent peers after a single trigger message.
  • Evaluates the attack on a controlled testbed across multiple LLM backends, multiple infection vectors, and multiple payload types, reporting a 64.5% aggregate success rate and sustained multi-hop propagation.
  • Analyzes architectural trust-boundary root causes and proposes defense strategies aimed at mitigating the identified vulnerabilities, noting that execution-level filtering may not stop propagation via tool/skill supply chains.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yihao Zhang', 'Zeming Wei', 'Xiaokun Luan', 'Chengcan Wu', 'Zhixin Zhang', 'Jiangrong Wu', 'Haolin Wu', 'Huanran Chen', 'Jun Sun', 'Meng Sun']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'Worm/malware propagation', 'Supply-chain attacks', 'Persistence & configuration hijacking']

item.title: LISAA: A Framework for Large Language Model Information Security Awareness Assessment
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes LISAA, a framework to assess large language model information security awareness (ISA) using 100 realistic security scenarios.
  • Evaluates models on a taxonomy of security topics with tension between implicit security cues and user satisfaction (i.e., refusal/unsafe-request handling).
  • Finds many deployed models have only medium-to-low ISA, including cases where cybersecurity-knowledge benchmarks do not correlate with ISA behavior.
  • Includes an online tool for evaluating new LLMs and highlights higher risk for smaller model variants.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research (Framework + Evaluation Tool)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ofir Cohen', 'Gil Ari Agmon', 'Asaf Shabtai', 'Rami Puzis']
  • Tags: ['LLM Safety', 'Security Evaluation', 'Red Teaming/Benchmarking', 'Adversarial & Unsafe Request Handling', 'Cybersecurity Risk Assessment']

item.title: StealthRL: Reinforcement Learning Paraphrase Attacks for Multi-Detector Evasion of AI-Text Detectors
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes StealthRL, an RL-based paraphrase attack framework to evade multiple AI-text detectors while preserving semantics.
  • Trains an adversarial paraphrase policy against a multi-detector ensemble and reports strong evasion performance across several detector families.
  • Includes transfer evaluation to held-out detectors, suggesting shared architectural vulnerabilities rather than brittle, detector-specific weaknesses.
  • Provides quantitative detector-robustness results (e.g., AUROC/TPR@FPR) plus LLM-based quality checks and distribution analyses to explain evasion success.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Suraj Ranganath', 'Atharv Ramesh']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial paraphrasing', 'AI-text detector evasion', 'Reinforcement learning attacks', 'Transferability']

item.title: Reinforcement Unlearning via Group Relative Policy Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PURGE: an LLM unlearning method to remove memorized sensitive/copyrighted information without retraining from scratch.
  • Frames unlearning as a verifiable problem using Group Relative Policy Optimization with an intrinsic reward that penalizes mention of forbidden concepts.
  • Reports improved efficiency (lower token usage), preservation of utility/fluency, and improved adversarial robustness, evaluated on the RWKU benchmark.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Efstratios Zaradoukas', 'Bardh Prenkaj', 'Gjergji Kasneci']
  • Tags: ['AI unlearning', 'privacy/memorization risk', 'reward shaping', 'RL-based fine-tuning']

item.title: KoALA: KL-L0 Adversarial Detector via Label Agreement
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes KoALA, a plug-and-play adversarial example detector that flags attacks via disagreement between two similarity metrics (KL divergence and an L0-based similarity).
  • Designed to detect different perturbation regimes (dense low-amplitude vs sparse high-impact changes) without architecture changes or adversarial retraining.
  • Requires only lightweight fine-tuning on clean data to align embeddings with both metrics and provides a correctness proof.
  • Evaluates on image classification with ResNet/CIFAR-10 and multimodal CLIP/Tiny-ImageNet, reporting strong detection precision/recall.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Siqi Li', 'Yasser Shoukry']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-detection', 'adversarial-examples', 'robustness', 'input/label-agreement']

item.title: The Autonomy Tax: Defense Training Breaks LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes how defense training for LLM agents against prompt injection affects agent tool-using competence.
  • Finds a capability-alignment paradox: defended models often become incompetent at multi-step tasks and fail more frequently than undefended baselines.
  • Evaluates across 97 agent tasks and 1,000 adversarial prompts, identifying three defense-specific failure biases (agent incompetence, cascade amplification, trigger bias).
  • Provides root-cause evidence that models shortcut-learn surface attack patterns rather than developing semantic threat understanding.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shawn Li', 'Yue Zhao']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'Prompt injection', 'Adversarial evaluation', 'Defense training', 'Agent security']

item.title: Automated Membership Inference Attacks: Discovering MIA Signal Computations using LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces AutoMIA, a framework that uses LLM agents to automate the design/implementation of membership inference attack (MIA) signal computations.
  • Systematically searches a space of potential attack strategies to find new, target-specific MIAs.
  • Evaluates on configurable target models/datasets and reports improved attack performance (up to 0.18 absolute AUC over existing MIAs).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Toan Tran', 'Olivera Kotevska', 'Li Xiong']
  • Tags: ['membership inference', 'privacy attacks', 'LLM agents', 'model information leakage']

item.title: A Novel Solution for Zero-Day Attack Detection in IDS using Self-Attention and Jensen-Shannon Divergence in WGAN-GP
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SA-WGAN-GP/JS-WGAN-GP/SA-JS-WGAN-GP to synthesize network-traffic samples that mimic zero-day attack patterns for training IDS models.
  • Uses self-attention to capture long-range cross-feature dependencies in generated traffic and Jensen–Shannon divergence (auxiliary discriminator) to regularize GAN training for smoother gradients and better sample quality.
  • Evaluates “zero-day risk detection” via a leave-one-attack-type-out protocol on NSL-KDD, where an attack type is held out during training to emulate unknown attacks.
  • Reports improved IDS performance and effectiveness at detecting/flagging held-out (emulated) zero-day behavior.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ziyu Mu', 'Xiyu Shi', 'Safak Dogan']
  • Tags: ['intrusion detection', 'zero-day attack detection', 'GAN-based data augmentation', 'self-attention', 'WGAN-GP']

item.title: Trojan horse hunt in deep forecasting models: Insights from the European Space Agency competition
item.description:
Summary

  • Examines trojan horse (backdoor) security risks in deep time-series forecasting models for spacecraft telemetry.
  • Focuses on detecting hidden trigger patterns planted in training data or model weights (a red-teaming/detection setting).
  • Presents a competition-based benchmark: task formulation, dataset/benchmark set, evaluation protocol, and best solutions/insights.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking / Research (competition report)

item.title: ARMOR: Adaptive Resilience Against Model Poisoning Attacks in Continual Federated Learning for Mobile Indoor Localization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ARMOR, a continual federated learning framework for mobile indoor localization that aims to resist adversarial model poisoning.
  • Uses a state-space model (SSM) to predict the expected next state of global model weight tensors, flagging incoming client updates that deviate from this prediction.
  • Detects deviations and selectively mitigates corrupted updates before aggregation to prevent global model corruption and performance degradation.
  • Evaluated on real-world mobile/device settings, reporting significant error reductions and demonstrating resilience under model poisoning.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Danish Gufran', 'Akhil Singampalli', 'Sudeep Pasricha']
  • Tags: ['model poisoning', 'continual federated learning', 'attack detection', 'robust aggregation']

item.title: Neural Uncertainty Principle: A Unified View of Adversarial Fragility and LLM Hallucination
item.description:
Summary

  • Unifies adversarial fragility (vision) and LLM hallucination (language) under a single geometric/uncertainty principle tied to loss-gradient conjugacy.
  • Introduces a single-backward probe (input-gradient correlation channel) to detect hallucination risk without generating tokens and to diagnose robustness issues.
  • Proposes defenses that do not rely on adversarial training: ConjMask (mask high-contribution components) for robustness and LogitReg (logit-side regularization) for reliability.
  • Frames robustness/halucination as an uncertainty-budget tradeoff in near-bound regimes and studies how compression and prompt-gradient coupling affect failure modes.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Dong-Xiao Zhang', 'Hu Lou', 'Jun-Jie Zhang', 'Jun Zhu', 'Deyu Meng']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'hallucination detection', 'input-gradient analysis', 'defense/regularization']

item.title: The Phish, The Spam, and The Valid: Generating Feature-Rich Emails for Benchmarking LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces PhishFuzzer, a metadata-enriched framework for generating diverse email variants labeled as Phishing, Spam, or Valid.
  • Seeds real emails into LLMs to create structurally consistent variants with controlled entity and length dimensions, including full URL and attachment metadata.
  • Uses the generated dataset to benchmark LLMs for reliability/robustness under Basic vs Full settings and evaluates impact of structural metadata on detection accuracy using task success/confidence metrics.
  • Provides an open-source dataset and generation framework intended for benchmarking next-generation email security systems.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

  • Authors: ['Rebeka Toth', 'Tamas Bisztray', 'Nils Gruschka']
  • Tags: ['email-security', 'LLM-based generation', 'phishing/spam detection', 'benchmarking-dataset', 'robustness-evaluation']

item.description:
Summary

  • Develops and evaluates adversarial attack methods for cross-site scripting (XSS) detectors using deep reinforcement learning and mutation-based strategies.
  • Replicates prior state-of-the-art XSS adversarial attacks and analyzes threats to evaluation validity in the reference work.
  • Introduces an “XSS Oracle” to mitigate threats to validity and improve evaluation effectiveness.
  • Reports high model evasion/escape performance (escape rate >96%) when validity threats are addressed.

Paper Type

  • Research (Evaluation/Extension)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Samuele Pasini', 'Gianluca Maragliano', 'Jinhan Kim', 'Paolo Tonella']
  • Tags: ['web security', 'adversarial ML', 'reinforcement learning', 'XSS detection evasion']

item.title: LISAA: A Framework for Large Language Model Information Security Awareness Assessment
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes LISAA, a framework to assess large language model information security awareness (ISA) using 100 realistic security scenarios.
  • Evaluates models on a taxonomy of security topics with tension between implicit security cues and user satisfaction (i.e., refusal/unsafe-request handling).
  • Finds many deployed models have only medium-to-low ISA, including cases where cybersecurity-knowledge benchmarks do not correlate with ISA behavior.
  • Includes an online tool for evaluating new LLMs and highlights higher risk for smaller model variants.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research (Framework + Evaluation Tool)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ofir Cohen', 'Gil Ari Agmon', 'Asaf Shabtai', 'Rami Puzis']
  • Tags: ['LLM Safety', 'Security Evaluation', 'Red Teaming/Benchmarking', 'Adversarial & Unsafe Request Handling', 'Cybersecurity Risk Assessment']

item.title: From Masks to Pixels and Meaning: A New Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Metrics for VLM Image Tampering
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces a taxonomy and pixel-level benchmark for VLM image tampering that moves beyond mask-based evaluation to per-pixel tamper maps and semantic supervision.
  • Proposes a training framework and evaluation metrics that measure pixel-level correctness/localization and also assess “tamper meaning” via semantic classification and language descriptions.
  • Re-evaluates existing mask-based tampering detectors and shows significant metric misalignment and failure modes (micro-edits, off-mask changes).

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking + Research (taxonomy/metrics/framework)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xinyi Shang', 'Yi Tang', 'Jiacheng Cui', 'Ahmed Elhagry', 'Salwa K. Al Khatib', 'Sondos Mahmoud Bsharat', 'Jiacheng Liu', 'Xiaohan Zhao', 'Jing-Hao Xue', 'Hao Li', 'Salman Khan', 'Zhiqiang Shen']
  • Tags: ['Vision-Language Security', 'Image Tampering Detection', 'Localization & Pixel-Level Evaluation', 'Benchmark/Benchmarking']

item.title: Evolving Jailbreaks: Automated Multi-Objective Long-Tail Attacks on Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes EvoJail, an automated framework using multi-objective evolutionary search to discover long-tail distribution jailbreak prompts for LLMs.
  • Optimizes for both jailbreak effectiveness and low output perplexity, using a semantic-algorithmic representation that captures semantic intent and encryption/decryption-like structural transformations.
  • Uses LLM-assisted evolutionary operators for adaptive mutation/crossover to explore a large, open-ended search space.
  • Demonstrates that EvoJail finds diverse, effective long-tail jailbreak strategies and matches/competes with existing approaches at individual and ensemble levels.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenjing Hong', 'Zhonghua Rong', 'Li Wang', 'Feng Chang', 'Jian Zhu', 'Ke Tang', 'Zexuan Zhu', 'Yew-Soon Ong']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'prompt injection/attack prompting', 'automated adversarial search', 'long-tail attacks']

item.title: Trojan's Whisper: Stealthy Manipulation of OpenClaw through Injected Bootstrapped Guidance
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a new attack surface in autonomous coding agents (OpenClaw) via “guidance injection” using injected bootstrapped guidance/lifecycle hooks.
  • Introduces and evaluates 26 malicious skills across 13 attack categories (e.g., credential exfiltration, workspace destruction, privilege escalation, persistent backdoors).
  • Proposes ORE-Bench to evaluate attacks across 52 user prompts and six LLM backends; reports success rates up to 64.2%.
  • Finds 94% of malicious skills evade existing static and LLM-based scanners; argues for defenses like capability isolation, runtime policy enforcement, and guidance provenance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Fazhong Liu', 'Zhuoyan Chen', 'Tu Lan', 'Haozhen Tan', 'Zhenyu Xu', 'Xiang Li', 'Guoxing Chen', 'Yan Meng', 'Haojin Zhu']
  • Tags: ['Guidance injection', 'Autonomous coding agents', 'Malicious skills', 'Backdoors/privilege escalation', 'Security evaluation/benchmarks']

item.title: ARMOR: Adaptive Resilience Against Model Poisoning Attacks in Continual Federated Learning for Mobile Indoor Localization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ARMOR, a continual federated learning framework for mobile indoor localization that aims to resist adversarial model poisoning.
  • Uses a state-space model (SSM) to predict the expected next state of global model weight tensors, flagging incoming client updates that deviate from this prediction.
  • Detects deviations and selectively mitigates corrupted updates before aggregation to prevent global model corruption and performance degradation.
  • Evaluated on real-world mobile/device settings, reporting significant error reductions and demonstrating resilience under model poisoning.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Danish Gufran', 'Akhil Singampalli', 'Sudeep Pasricha']
  • Tags: ['model poisoning', 'continual federated learning', 'attack detection', 'robust aggregation']

item.title: AI Psychosis: Does Conversational AI Amplify Delusion-Related Language?
item.description:
Summary

  • Examines whether multi-turn conversational AI amplifies delusion-related language over time.
  • Creates simulated users from Reddit longitudinal histories and measures delusion intensity using a proposed DelusionScore across conversation turns.
  • Finds increased delusion-related language trajectories for users with prior delusion-related discourse, with stronger effects for reality skepticism and compulsive reasoning themes.
  • Shows that conditioning model responses on the current DelusionScore can substantially reduce these trajectories, suggesting a state-aware safety mitigation approach.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Soorya Ram Shimgekar', 'Vipin Gunda', 'Jiwon Kim', 'Violeta J. Rodriguez', 'Hari Sundaram', 'Koustuv Saha']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'Mental health risk', 'Adversarial safety evaluation (state-aware)', 'Language-based vulnerability measurement']

item.title: A Framework for Formalizing LLM Agent Security
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a framework for contextual security in LLM agents using four security properties: task alignment, action alignment, source authorization, and data isolation.
  • Reformalizes multiple LLM agent attacks (e.g., indirect/direct prompt injection, jailbreak, task drift, memory poisoning) as specific violations of these properties.
  • Reformalizes defenses as mechanisms that strengthen verification/oracle functions and/or check security property violations during execution.
  • Introduces oracle functions to verify whether security properties are violated as an agent executes a task.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Vincent Siu', 'Jingxuan He', 'Kyle Montgomery', 'Zhun Wang', 'Neil Gong', 'Chenguang Wang', 'Dawn Song']
  • Tags: ['LLM agent security', 'Prompt injection/jailbreaks', 'Security formalization', 'Verification/oracle-based defenses']

item.title: The Autonomy Tax: Defense Training Breaks LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes how defense training for LLM agents against prompt injection affects agent tool-using competence.
  • Finds a capability-alignment paradox: defended models often become incompetent at multi-step tasks and fail more frequently than undefended baselines.
  • Evaluates across 97 agent tasks and 1,000 adversarial prompts, identifying three defense-specific failure biases (agent incompetence, cascade amplification, trigger bias).
  • Provides root-cause evidence that models shortcut-learn surface attack patterns rather than developing semantic threat understanding.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shawn Li', 'Yue Zhao']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'Prompt injection', 'Adversarial evaluation', 'Defense training', 'Agent security']

item.title: A Novel Solution for Zero-Day Attack Detection in IDS using Self-Attention and Jensen-Shannon Divergence in WGAN-GP
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SA-WGAN-GP/JS-WGAN-GP/SA-JS-WGAN-GP to synthesize network-traffic samples that mimic zero-day attack patterns for training IDS models.
  • Uses self-attention to capture long-range cross-feature dependencies in generated traffic and Jensen–Shannon divergence (auxiliary discriminator) to regularize GAN training for smoother gradients and better sample quality.
  • Evaluates “zero-day risk detection” via a leave-one-attack-type-out protocol on NSL-KDD, where an attack type is held out during training to emulate unknown attacks.
  • Reports improved IDS performance and effectiveness at detecting/flagging held-out (emulated) zero-day behavior.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ziyu Mu', 'Xiyu Shi', 'Safak Dogan']
  • Tags: ['intrusion detection', 'zero-day attack detection', 'GAN-based data augmentation', 'self-attention', 'WGAN-GP']

item.title: LSR: Linguistic Safety Robustness Benchmark for Low-Resource West African Languages
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces LSR, a cross-lingual safety robustness benchmark for low-resource West African languages (Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Igala).
  • Evaluates refusal degradation when harmful intent is expressed in target languages, using matched English vs target-language probes.
  • Proposes Refusal Centroid Drift (RCD) to quantify loss of English refusal behavior across languages and harm categories.
  • Implements the benchmark in Inspect AI and provides public dataset/reference implementation.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Godwin Abuh Faruna']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'adversarial evaluation', 'jailbreak/attack probes', 'cross-lingual robustness']

item.title: When Prompt Optimization Becomes Jailbreaking: Adaptive Red-Teaming of Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies adaptive, automated prompt optimization that effectively performs jailbreaking on LLMs.
  • Uses black-box prompt refinement via DSPy with an evaluator-based danger score to search for safety failures.
  • Demonstrates large increases in danger scores (e.g., Qwen 3 8B from 0.09 to 0.79) compared to baseline and highlights limitations of static safety benchmarks.
  • Argues that adaptive red-teaming is necessary for more realistic safety evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zafir Shamsi', 'Nikhil Chekuru', 'Zachary Guzman', 'Shivank Garg']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'adaptive red-teaming', 'prompt optimization', 'black-box adversarial attacks']
